title: Adjusting Entries
description: Accruals, deferrals, depreciation and other adjustments.
html:
Why do we need adjusting entries?

Some revenues and expenses are not recorded at exactly the same time cash is received or paid.

At the end of an accounting period, adjusting entries help make sure revenues and expenses are recognized in the appropriate period under accrual accounting.

Common adjusting entries

  • Accrued revenues
  • Accrued expenses
  • Prepaid expenses
  • Unearned revenue
  • Depreciation

1. Accrued Expenses

An accrued expense is an expense that has been incurred but has not yet been paid or recorded.

Example — Wages

Employees have earned $2,000 by December 31, but they will be paid in January.

2. Prepaid Expenses

A prepaid expense begins as an asset because the company has paid for a future benefit.

As that benefit is used, part of the asset becomes an expense.

Example — Insurance

A company originally pays $12,000 for 12 months of insurance.

After one month, $1,000 has been used.

3. Unearned Revenue

When a customer pays before the company has earned the revenue, the company initially records a liability.

As the service is performed, the liability decreases and revenue is recognized.

Example

A company previously received $5,000 in advance. By period-end, it has earned $2,000.

4. Depreciation

Long-lived assets such as equipment generally provide benefits over multiple accounting periods.

Depreciation allocates the asset's depreciable cost over its useful life.

Simple Example

Assume equipment has a depreciable amount of $12,000 and that $1,000 of depreciation should be recognized for the current period.

The big idea

Adjusting entries help put revenues and expenses into the appropriate accounting period.

quiz.prompt: Employees earned $4,000 of wages before year-end, but the company will pay them next year. What should the company record?

choices.text: Debit Wages Expense; Credit Wages Payable
No entry until the employees are paid

quiz.explanation: The wages were incurred in the current period. Wages Expense is debited and Wages Payable is credited.
